alignments.note: אִישׁ distributive rendered every man; every is the ASV's completion of the distributive sense and joins the noun's unit, headed on man, which carries the lexeme (rule 31).
Emphatic possessive his own belongs whole to the suffix, headed on the pronoun (rule 18).
No article morpheme is segmented here, so the supplied the joins the nominal expression it determines (rule 15), headed on ensigns.
The lamed takes the of the ASV writes for the relation (rule 11).
Construct noun to houses; the English possessive puts the determiner on the possessor, so nothing else is owed here (rule 29).
Imperfect with its auxiliary; head on the lexical verb (rule 24).
Construct noun with the supplied the (rules 15, 29), headed on children.
Nomen rectum takes the relational of (rule 19).

מִנֶּגֶד is a preposition before a construct noun rendered by the single compound English preposition over against, so the pair fuses under rule 30's one-rendering reading; head on against, which carries נֶגֶד's lexeme (rule 24). The competing reading gives over to מִן and against to נֶגֶד, but no morpheme owns a part of a compound preposition.
סָבִיב takes the whole compound adverb round about, headed on round, exactly as rule 40 directs.
The lamed after סָבִיב is left with no English of its own; the compound round about is the adverb's whole rendering and is not divided to feed it (rule 40, which cites this very construction).
Construct noun with a supplied the, since no article morpheme is present (rule 29).
Nomen rectum with the relational of (rule 19).
Repeated finite verb with its subject pronoun and auxiliary (rule 17), headed on the lexical verb.

review_notes: The two occurrences of יַחֲנוּ are separately written and separately rendered, so rule 22 does not reach either.
מִנֶּגֶד fused under rule 30; the split reading is named in that unit's note.
